paragraph: The single-family market in Wood-Ridge produced 20 sales over six months at a median of $699,500, with a sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00, 45 percent of homes going above asking, and a median of 27.5 days on market. That is competitive but not frenzied. Priced homes move, and buyers still have room to think. Condos and townhouses are the larger share of activity here with 31 sales at a median of $730,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.012, and 24 days on market. That median sitting above the single-family median is uncommon in Bergen County, and it tells you this category is carrying substantial newer attached product rather than small older units. Sales ran from $355,000 to $958,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. On the seasonal read, condo volume climbed into July while the monthly median dropped from $850,000 in June to $647,000, which points to a shift in what closed, not a drop in values. Single-family months are too thin to read a trend from. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse.
